23->30 (band=mild_tachypneic)
A 57-year-old male with a history of BPH on prazosin and tadalafil presents to the ED with acute
urinary retention and suprapubic pain that has persisted for 3 hours. Vital signs: blood pressure
179/116 mm Hg, pulse 85/min, respiratory rate 30/min, temperature 36.5 degrees celcius. On physical
examination, he has suprapubic tenderness. After catheterization of 700 ml urine, the following
laboratory values were obtained: | **Initial** | | **After 8 hours** | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Serum potassium |
4.2 mmol/L | Serum potassium | 4.0 mmol/L | | Serum sodium | 140 mmol/L | Serum sodium | 142
mmol/L | | Serum chloride | 102 mmol/L | Serum chloride | 110 mmol/L | | Serum creatinine | 1.4 mg/dL |
Serum creatinine | 1.6 mg/dL | | Serum blood urea nitrogen | 64 mg/dL | Serum blood urea nitrogen | 62
mg/dL | | Urine output | (drained 700 ml) | Urine output | 260 mL | The patient weighs 84 kg and is 175
centimeters tall. A nephrology consultation is recommended. Which of the following parameters best
supports this recommendation? Answer Choices: (A) Urine specific gravity (B) BUN/Creatinine ratio (C)
Serum creatinine (SCr) (D) Urine output (E) Fractional excretion of sodium (FENa) (F) Serum chloride
trend (G) Urine osmolality (H) Serum blood urea nitrogen (BUN) (I) Estimated glomerular filtration rate
(eGFR) (J) Serum potassium trend
 A. Serum potassium trend
B. Urine output
C. Urine osmolality
D. Urine specific gravity
E. Serum chloride trend
F. Serum blood urea nitrogen (BUN)
G. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)
H. BUN/Creatinine ratio
I. Serum creatinine (SCr)
J. Fractional excretion of sodium (FENa)
